# Module 1 Knowledge Check {.unnumbered}

This knowledge check covers the key learning outcomes from Module 1: Getting Started. Test your understanding of pipetting techniques and volume measurement accuracy.

## Question 1: Pipette Volume Practice

When combining four 4 µL additions into a single spot on the practice card, what total volume should you predict before testing recovery?

- [ ] 4 µL
- [ ] 16 µL
- [ ] 8 µL
- [ ] 20 µL

## Question 2: Serial Dilution Factor

In the worked example in Module 1, 1 mL of inoculum is added to 9 mL of broth at each step. What is the dilution factor for each transfer?

- [ ] 1:5
- [ ] 1:10
- [ ] 1:100
- [ ] Variable


## Question 3: Micropipette Mixing

When mixing two liquids in a micropipette tip, what is the correct procedure?

- [ ] Press only to the first stop when drawing up, then release slowly
- [ ] Press all the way to the second stop each time
- [ ] Press to the first stop, then to the second stop together
- [ ] Use quick repeated motions to mix thoroughly


## Question 4: Serial Dilution Setup

In the crystal violet serial dilution protocol, how many microliters of water are pipetted into each well of row A?

- [ ] 25 µL
- [ ] 50 µL
- [ ] 100 µL
- [ ] 150 µL


## Question 5: Drop Collection Practice

When practicing the drop-collection exercise on the pipette practice card, what should you observe to assess pipetting consistency?

- [ ] Only whether drops stay within the circles
- [ ] The relative uniformity of drop size and volume consistency across replicate transfers
- [ ] The color intensity of the dye used
- [ ] How quickly the drops evaporate


---

**Review these learning outcomes to deepen your understanding:**

- Explain how streak plating helps dilute bacteria
- Identify the features of mechanical micropipettes
- Collect and interpret pipetting data
- Create a team charter and communication plan

**Next Steps:** If you found any questions challenging, revisit those sections in Module 1 and practice the corresponding techniques in lab.
